text:
tasha: heads up — around 12:07 we saw a sustained GPU allocation spike from tenant acme-search in us-east-1. routing pushed a bunch of warm slots into eu-west as fallback and we hit cross-region egress + queueing.
ops-bot: ALERT: akku.provision.gpu_util > 92% (us-east-1), p95 latency for gen route +1200ms, fallback routing enabled.
maria: is this dedicated or shared?
tasha: dedicated pool for acme-search but their burst outgrew slice and our fallback kicked in to keep SLOs.
ajay: that cross-region stitch is expensive. did we spill to preemptible in us-west or to eu-west?
tasha: eu-west, because preemptible policy had no compatible quantized variant for that model.
kevin: cost hit estimate?
tasha: rough calc: ~0.9 GPU-hours + 600GB egress -> ~$850 this one hour.
linh: we should avoid cross-region fallbacks unless warm-pool cold ratio > 2. current router policy is too eager.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: add a soft-quarantine for noisy tenant -> hold them to local soft-rate until warm slots available, instead of hopping regions. Lower immediate SLO but saves cost and egress.
ajay: Alternatively we could stitch a transient local buffer pool using fractional slices from other dedicated tenants with throttled QoS. Need a safe policy for consent and cost recovery.
samir: both approaches valid. For short term, can we add a routing override that prefers: 1) local preemptible quantized variant, 2) local fractional slice, 3) cross-region fallback as last resort?
linh: +1. Here's a quick router policy snippet I cooked up:
```yaml
- match: tenant == "acme-search"
  prefer: [local_quantized, fractional_slice]
  fallback: [cross_region]
  soft_quarantine: true
  quarantine_ttl: 300s
```
maria: quarantine_ttl 300s might be too short for long warmups. maybe 10m.
kevin: we need to model customer impact. If we soft-quarantine, acme-search p99 might spike but p50/p90 stay ok. Finance wants egress prevented.
ajay: ops-sim shows egress cost reduces 4x if we avoid cross-region for same burst.
tasha: ops runbook note: when dedicated pool saturates, disable immediate cross-region burst unless explicit override.
ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-routing-fallback (added)
maria: small automation idea — when a tenant hits warm-slot depletion, send an automated message to tenant slack/webhook offering auto-quantize option or accept degraded latency. If no response, apply soft-quarantine.
samir: love that. how about adding a telemetry tag so Billing can allocate cross-region egress back to tenant automatically?
kevin: yes billing tagging is must. Also add an alert for repeated cross-region use per tenant per day.
linh: I'll open a PR for router change + unit tests. will also add an integration test to simulate warm-pool drain.
linh: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/498 (WIP)
ajay: quick mitigation script if this happens again tonight:
```bash
# move fallback priority off
curl -X POST $ROUTER/admin/override -d '{"tenant":"acme-search","priority":"local_only","ttl":600}'
```
tasha: running override now to stop more eu-west hops.
tasha: override accepted.
ops-bot: ACTION: ticket INFRA-3241 created: "Cross-region fallback gating + tenant soft-quarantine policy" assigned @linh @maria @kevin.
maria: will own work on quarantine semantics and billing tags.
linh: will push PR + tests tomorrow AM.
kevin: I'll run cost retros and add a daily alarm on cross-region egress per-tenant > $200.
samir: follow-up: we should audit model catalog for quantized variants per region to reduce future falls.
tasha: good call. For now, monitor acme-search, keep override on for 10m, and add follow-ups to INFRA-3241.
maria: noted. ping me if it repeats. :thumbsup:
